network.overall_strategy: The network synthesizes L-valine from simple C1 and C2 feedstocks (CO2, HCN, NH3, CH4) in a geochemically plausible, multi-environment process. Central intermediates such as α-ketoisovaleric acid and isobutyraldehyde are constructed via Strecker, Reductive Amination, and Aldol pathways, making use of mineral-catalyzed carbon fixation (e.g., pyruvate synthesis), followed by amination in both hydrothermal and surface environments. Multiple routes leverage hydrothermal and surface minerals, with wet-dry cycles, and prebiotic pools to promote both carbon–carbon bond formation and nitrogen incorporation, ultimately converging at valine through diverse chemical logic.

reactions.name: Reverse Krebs: Reductive reconversion of methane and CO2 to pyruvate
reactions.mechanism: Mineral-catalyzed chain growth using Fe/Ni-sulfur clusters facilitating reduction and C–C coupling.
reactions.reasoning: Reverse Krebs-like carboxylations on Fe/Ni sulfides demonstrated in hydrothermal simulation experiments (Cody et al., 2000; Huber & Wächtershäuser, 1997).

reactions.name: Aldol addition: Formaldehyde and pyruvate to lactic acid
reactions.mechanism: Aldol condensation of an aldehyde (formaldehyde) with a carbonyl (pyruvate) facilitated by clay mineral surfaces.
reactions.reasoning: Surface-catalyzed aldol chemistry is demonstrated (Pizzarello et al., 2012; Ertem & Ferris, 1997). Clays increase yields and selectivity.

reactions.name: Reduction of pyruvate to lactic acid
reactions.mechanism: Hydrogenation at mineral surface reduces carbonyl of pyruvate to hydroxy group.
reactions.reasoning: Prebiotic reduction of keto acids via H2 on Fe-oxide minerals is widely supported (Cody et al., 2001).

reactions.name: Aldol addition: Pyruvate with acetone to alpha-ketoisovalerate
reactions.mechanism: Aldol addition of acetone with pyruvate on clay surface leads to 3-methyl-2-oxobutanoic acid.
reactions.reasoning: Clays catalyze aldol/Claisen-like couplings in evaporative pools (Ertem & Ferris, 1997).

reactions.name: Hydrothermal conversion of lactic acid to acetone
reactions.mechanism: Mineral-catalyzed dehydration and decarboxylation yields acetone from lactic acid.
reactions.reasoning: Hydrothermal decarboxylations/dehydrations shown for hydroxy acids (Shock, 1992; Cody, 2001).

reactions.name: Reductive amination of alpha-ketoisovaleric acid to valine (racemic)
reactions.mechanism: Mineral-catalyzed reductive amination of keto acid with ammonia and H2 yields racemic valine.
reactions.reasoning: Reductive amination over FeS/NiS minerals plausible prebiotically (Kitani et al., 2015; Martin & Russell, 2007); chirality undetermined.

reactions.name: Surface Strecker synthesis of valine
reactions.mechanism: Addition of HCN to isobutyraldehyde followed by hydrolysis and amination yields valine (racemate).
reactions.reasoning: Strecker synthesis demonstrated for various amino acids on phosphate/borate minerals (Cleaves, 2010; Saladino et al., 2012).

reactions.name: Rac-valine to L-valine
agents: chiral surface (montmorillonite or lipid vesicle membrane)
reactions.mechanism: Chiral selection or imprinted mineral adsorption favors L-valine enrichment or resolution.
reactions.reasoning: Chiral mineral surfaces and lipid vesicles promote enantioenrichment (Soai et al., 1995; Hazen et al., 2001; speculative for early Earth).

reactions.name: Aldol: Acetone with formaldehyde to isobutyraldehyde
reactions.reasoning: Aldol branch formation demonstrated on evaporative surfaces (Kim et al., 2011; Camprubi et al., 2017).

reactions.name: Nitrile hydrolysis: Isobutyronitrile to alpha-ketoisovaleric acid
reactions.mechanism: Hydrolysis of nitrile and subsequent oxidation to yields keto acid.
reactions.reasoning: Nitrile hydrolysis is mineral-catalyzed and works in hydrothermal and acidic vent contexts (LaRowe & Regnier, 2008).

reactions.name: Amination of isovaleric acid to valine amine intermediate
reactions.mechanism: Amination of carboxylic acid under reductive mineral-catalyzed conditions.
reactions.reasoning: Amination of aliphatic acids demonstrated on iron minerals (Preiner et al., 2020, speculative for direct route here).

reactions.name: Oxidation of valine amine to valine
reactions.mechanism: Oxidative conversion of amine to α-amino acid.
reactions.reasoning: Oxidative amine to amino acid conversion on Fe minerals is plausible, though not yet directly shown for valine; speculative but justified by analogous chemistries.

reactions.name: Chain elongation: Propanal aldol with formaldehyde to butanal
reactions.mechanism: Aldol chain elongation extends C3 to C4 aldehyde.
reactions.reasoning: Surface promoted chain elongation observed for simple aldehydes (Kim et al., 2011).

reactions.name: Methyl branching: Butanal with methylation to isobutyraldehyde
reactions.mechanism: Mineral catalyzed methyl transfer from methane to form branched aldehyde.
reactions.reasoning: Prebiotic methylation demonstrated for branched precursor synthesis (Kitadai et al., 2017, speculative for C4→branched C4 transformation).

reactions.name: Direct Strecker on butanal (alternative route)
reactions.mechanism: Standard Strecker on straight-chain aldehyde yields isobutyronitrile (followed by branching).
reactions.reasoning: Strecker synthesis adaptable to various aldehydes (Saladino et al., 2012).

pathways.name: Strecker Pathway via Isobutyraldehyde
pathways.description: Surface Strecker synthesis from isobutyraldehyde via HCN to rac-valine followed by enantioenrichment.

pathways.name: Reductive Amination via Alpha-Ketoisovalerate
pathways.description: Hydrothermal and surface synthesis of alpha-ketoisovalerate, followed by FeS-catalyzed reductive amination.

pathways.name: Nitrile Hydrolysis via Isobutyronitrile
pathways.description: Surface formation of isobutyronitrile from isobutyraldehyde, followed by hydrothermal hydrolysis and amination to valine.

pathways.name: Direct amination of isovaleric acid route
pathways.description: Amination of isovaleric acid followed by oxidative conversion to valine.

pathways.name: Aldol Branching from Acetone and Pyruvate
pathways.description: Acetone and pyruvate condense to alpha-ketoisovalerate, leading through reductive amination.

pathways.name: Chain Elongation via Butanal
pathways.description: Propanal reacts to form butanal, which can be methylated or subjected to Strecker for branched intermediates to valine.

pathways.name: Strecker on Butanal plus Branching
pathways.description: Butanal made from propanal and formaldehyde undergoes Strecker route to isobutyronitrile, then hydrolyzes.

pathways.name: Lactic Acid to Acetone and Aldol Branching
pathways.description: Pyruvate reduced to lactic acid, which is transformed to acetone; acetone acts as branch donor in subsequent aldol.

pathways.name: Direct Pyruvate Surface Branching Pathway
pathways.description: Direct aldol coupling with pyruvate and acetone on surface leads to alpha-ketoisovalerate.

pathways.name: Retro-synthetic Combination via Propanal
pathways.description: Propanal serves as key hub to chain elongation and branching to yield isobutyraldehyde, then to valine.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: P1 (Strecker Pathway via Isobutyraldehyde) contains several unbalanced reactions: rxn_009 (Aldol), rxn_015 (Strecker on butanal), rxn_007 (Strecker synthesis of valine). These exhibit C, H, O and sometimes N discrepancies as flagged by the balance check, undermining chemical feasibility. The pathway logic is generally reasonable prebiotically, but conservation issues must be addressed for approval.
suggestions: Correct atom balance in Strecker steps.
Account for missing water, ammonia, or other inferred byproducts.
Confirm isobutyraldehyde/precursor formula and intermediate mapping.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: P2 (Reductive Amination via alpha-Ketoisovalerate) is strongly undermined by mass conservation failures: rxn_001 (Reverse Krebs to pyruvate), rxn_004 (Aldol to α-ketoisovalerate), and rxn_006 (Reductive amination), all noted as unbalanced with missing or surplus H, O, C units. These steps are crucial for the synthetic logic, and their correction is necessary.
suggestions: Explicitly include H2O/H2 evolution or uptake as needed for balancing.
Check the correctness of formula assignments for all intermediates.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: P3 attempts a nitrile hydrolysis route but features four consecutive unbalanced reactions (aldol, Strecker, nitrile hydrolysis, reductive amination). Major atom/charge conservation issues must be resolved for chemical feasibility.
suggestions: Fix mass/charge imbalances in all steps.
Make explicit all generated side-products (NH3, HCN, H2O, etc).

pathway_evaluations.feedback: P4 (direct amination of isovaleric acid) is concise but the first step (rxn_011, amination) is unbalanced, showing surplus O. Otherwise, logic is straightforward, but full compliance with elemental conservation is needed.
suggestions: Balance amination (possibly with H2O or O2 byproduct).
Clarify mechanism, intermediate stoichiometry.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: P5 passes through several strongly unbalanced nodes: aldol, reduction, further aldol, and amination, each flagged for elemental mismatches. Feasibility is low until all equations are rectified.
suggestions: Check all Aldol/adduct stoichiometry.
Include water or other by-products explicitly.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: P6 (Chain Elongation) is particularly problematic with multiple deeply unbalanced reactions (notably rxn_014, methyl branching, which can't be balanced by simple co-reactants/products). Chemistry before Strecker addition is especially questionable here.
suggestions: Clarify how methyl branching occurs (indicate proper leaving groups, re-examine intermediates).
Address substantial C and H excess indicated.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: P7 recapitulates many of P6's problematic carbon skeleton rearrangements (rxn_014, rxn_013), presenting significant atom imbalances, alongside Strecker steps requiring adjustment.
suggestions: Fix all unbalanced steps.
Reassess scaffolding for four-carbon to branched intermediates.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: P8 routes through lactic acid and subsequent steps, but contains five unbalanced, chemically problematic steps (reduction, aldol, conversion to acetone, C–C assembly, and amination) prior to final chiral selection. Consider stepwise balance for all transformations.
suggestions: Correct all group transfer steps.
Check lactic acid/acetone interconversion.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: P9 (Direct Pyruvate Surface Branching) is concise yet relies on four consecutive unbalanced reactions including reverse Krebs pyruvate formation, thus needing rebalancing for physical plausibility.
suggestions: Re-balance all pyruvate-related conversion steps.
State byproducts explicitly.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: P10 recycles the problematic steps from the chain elongation and Strecker pathways, including severely unbalanced C- and H-transfer reactions (rxn_013, rxn_014, rxn_015) and Strecker logic requiring explicit balance.
suggestions: Fix all step balances.
Justify or redesign chain rearrangement chemistry.

evaluation.network_feedback: This network shows sophisticated synthetic design and offers multiple plausible prebiotic logic routes to valine, but suffers from critical failures in chemical feasibility due to severe and pervasive atom/charge balance violations in almost every reaction (as per the RDKit deterministic check). Many core steps (e.g., all Strecker, aldol, reductive amination, and C–C branching steps) are flagged, often with multiple atoms unaccounted for, and some reactions cannot be balanced with common byproducts. While most transformations are justified in terms of geochemical plausibility and environmental progression, chemical feasibility is strongly compromised. Substantial revision is required: each reaction must be explicitly mass- and charge-balanced, all side products shown, with clear intermediate assignments. Only then can this innovative network be appraised as viable. At present, due to conservation failures, approval cannot be granted.
